acceptance_criteria.criterion: All types and constants are exported from orchestration.types.ts.
OrchestrationResult.results is an array of per-repository outcomes with success/failure and optional error message.
BranchSwitchResult.results is a record keyed by repository ID with success, conflict, and optional error fields.
Timeout constants are numeric values in milliseconds.

summary: Created src/orchestration/orchestration.types.ts with all required type definitions and timeout constants. Defined OrchestrationRepoResult (per-repo clone outcome array element), OrchestrationResult (aggregate with results array), BranchSwitchRepoResult (per-repo branch-switch outcome), BranchSwitchResult (aggregate keyed Record), CLONE_TIMEOUT_MS (120000ms), and FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS (30000ms). TypeScript compiles with zero errors; all 244 existing tests pass.

summary: Code review PASS. The orchestration.types.ts file is clean, minimal, and well-documented. All four acceptance criteria are met. JSDoc is thorough: every export has a block comment, every property has an inline comment. camelCase property naming is consistent with the git/infra layer convention (vs. PascalCase used in model/storage layer) — the correct tier for this file. CLONE_TIMEOUT_MS comment proactively flags the future AppConfig migration path. comments.note: No observations — code is clean and consistent. The CLONE_TIMEOUT_MS and FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS JSDoc comments proactively note the AppConfig migration path, which is a good practice for future-proofing.

[documentation-forward] orchestration.types.ts introduces two distinct aggregate result shapes: OrchestrationResult uses an array (order-preserving, natural for clone batches) while BranchSwitchResult uses Record<string, …> (O(1) lookup by repo ID, natural for branch-switch). The inline JSDoc explains each shape, but an architecture note in docs/ or a module-level comment block could help future implementers understand when to prefer each pattern for new orchestrator result types.
